positions.summary: No ISF-style wealth tax in Attal's programme. He promises to cut the deficit without raising taxes and opposes higher taxes on savings, life insurance and inheritance.
positions.nuance: No explicit statement on reinstating the ISF was retrieved. The code is inferred from his no-tax-rise platform and his opposition to the Zucman tax (see eco2).

positions.summary: The Assemblée rejected the Zucman tax (2% on fortunes over EUR 100m) on 31 Oct 2025 by 228 to 172. The bloc central, which includes the Renaissance group Attal chairs, opposed it and called it a 'mirage'.
positions.nuance: Group-level vote. Attal's personal roll-call vote was not checked on datan/assemblee-nationale. He commented after the rejection (BFM, 31 Oct 2025) that a compromise 'ne plaît pas à tout le monde'. A 2026 Le Figaro piece on candidates' tax plans (paywalled) was not read.

positions.summary: Attal's 'droit au brut' lowers social contributions (the programme names employee charges, 'charges salariales') to raise net pay. He also says labour costs should not have risen since 2024. No pledge to cut production taxes or employer contributions specifically was found.
positions.nuance: Partial support. The statement names production taxes and employer contributions. His flagship cut targets employee contributions; he opposes raising employer costs but does not clearly pledge to lower them.

positions.summary: No evidence found on national tariffs or quotas to protect French sectors.
positions.nuance: A brief search found nothing. His economic federalism ('disparition totale des frontières économiques' within an EU core) points away from national tariffs, but that is not coded.

positions.summary: No evidence found on bringing energy or motorways back under public control.
positions.nuance: A brief search found nothing. The dette-écologique programme page discusses energy independence but does not mention EDF or nationalisation.

positions.summary: Opposes any rise in inheritance taxation and wants to make lifetime gifts easier and smoother (to grandchildren, great-nephews and great-nieces).
positions.nuance: Partial support. No explicit cut to inheritance tax rates; he blocks increases and eases gift transfers.

positions.summary: Wants to abolish the legal retirement age and move to a universal system based on contribution duration, with a real penalty for leaving early and a real bonus for leaving late. He rejects parametric fixes, so he does not support returning to 62.
positions.nuance: His current position (abolish the legal age) replaces the earlier defence of the 2023 reform at 64. The 2023 reform has since been suspended at 62 years and 9 months. Without a legal age, early departure would still be possible, but with a strong penalty.

positions.summary: Rejects raising the legal age (he called Philippe's 65 plan 'palliative care' and said 'On n'en est plus à bouger les paramètres'). He prefers abolishing the legal age, with a penalty/bonus system based on contribution duration.
positions.nuance: Coded -1, not -2: he opposes a higher legal age, but his system aims to make people work longer through strong penalties and bonuses.

positions.summary: Proposes a universal system 'avec une part de capitalisation' ('a real capitalisation pillar'), a state-funded EUR 1,000 retirement savings plan per child, and 50% of profit-sharing directed to retirement savings plans.
positions.nuance: Sources do not say whether the capitalisation part would be mandatory. If it is built into the universal system it could be compulsory, which would make it +2. Kept at +1 until the mechanism is confirmed.

positions.summary: Zero deficit in at most 10 years (balanced budget by 2037), up to EUR 150bn in savings, no tax rises, and a voluntary-departure plan for 100,000 civil servants. As PM in 2024 he cut ministry budgets by EUR 10bn.
positions.nuance: His target (zero deficit) is stricter than the 3% threshold. He frames it as 'rigoureuse et sérieuse' rather than austerity.

positions.summary: Pledges to cut 100,000 civil-service posts through a voluntary-departure plan with a severance bonus, and to remove one layer of local government.
positions.nuance: Reached through attrition and voluntary departures. Education, the armed forces, justice and the interior are reportedly spared.

positions.summary: Treats national debt as a loss of sovereignty and targets zero deficit. He backs EU-level common debt for climate adaptation.
positions.nuance: Opposes more national debt but is open to joint EU borrowing for climate, so partial opposition (-1).

positions.summary: No constitutional golden rule found. His fiscal plan includes 'impunité budgétaire zéro' with sanctions, which is not a constitutional deficit cap.
positions.nuance: A brief search (Le Monde/Le Parisien headlines of 2 July 2026) found no golden-rule pledge.

positions.summary: Raises wages through productivity and lower contributions ('droit au brut': +EUR 250 net for a EUR 2,200 net salary), not through faster SMIC increases.
positions.nuance: No pledge to raise the SMIC above inflation. Not explicitly opposed either, hence -1.

positions.summary: As PM (March 2024) he proposed cutting the maximum benefit duration (to no less than 12 months, from 18) and tightening eligibility. His 2027 programme promises an unemployment insurance reform that 'incite au travail' and saves over EUR 4bn.
positions.nuance: The 2027 programme does not specify duration or amount cuts, so confidence is medium. The 2024 tightening was halted after the dissolution.

positions.summary: As Prime Minister he supported extending the RSA reform that requires at least 15 hours per week of activity. This obligation is now in force, and nothing suggests he wants to abolish it.
positions.nuance: The only source is a secondary one (Wikipedia), so confidence is low. The campaign programme pages do not mention the RSA. His programme also stresses social spending that 'incites activity', which is consistent with keeping the obligation. A primary 2025-2026 source is still needed.

positions.summary: Wants people to work more: remove the 220-hour annual overtime cap. Promotes a four-day week only as a reorganisation of existing hours, 'where possible'.
positions.nuance: The four-day week means flexible scheduling, not fewer hours.

positions.summary: 'Accueillir moins pour accueillir mieux': a Canada-style points system, family reunification to fall, work to become the first ground for immigration ahead of family and student immigration, and limiting quotas voted by Parliament every two years.
positions.nuance: He wants an overall reduction, but work immigration is prioritised rather than cut sharply, so partial support (+1).

positions.summary: Proposes an annual multi-question referendum day and limiting immigration quotas set by Parliament. No referendum specifically on immigration policy found.
positions.nuance: BFMTV/AFP (1 Aug 2026) reports annual referendums and 'quotas limitatifs', but not as a referendum topic. La Croix (3 Aug 2026, not fetchable) links 'référendums' and 'quotas migratoires' in its headline. Worth a check if accessible.

positions.nuance: Only campaign-site sources could be opened (web search budget exhausted); no independent outlet corroboration, but the position is consistent and stated in his own programme.

positions.nuance: Not verified with a live source; 'guarantee a ceasefire' is conditional on a ceasefire existing. His 2026 statements stress amplifying support but do not mention troops.

positions.summary: Renaissance is firmly Atlanticist; Attal's programme lists 'nos alliances' as a vector of power and extends nuclear deterrence to allies. Leaving NATO's integrated command is not part of his platform.

record.bio: Gabriel Attal (born 16 March 1989) is a Renaissance politician who started on the Socialist side and later joined Emmanuel Macron's movement. He held several government posts from 2018 and became France's youngest Prime Minister on 9 January 2024. President Macron accepted his resignation on 16 July 2024, after the June-July 2024 snap legislative elections. He then ran a caretaker government until Michel Barnier was appointed on 5 September 2024. He has chaired the Ensemble pour la République group in the Assemblée nationale since July 2024 and has been Renaissance general secretary since December 2024. He announced his 2027 presidential candidacy on 22 May 2026 in Mur-de-Barrez (Aveyron).
offices: Secretary of State to the Minister of National Education and Youth
Deputy, Hauts-de-Seine 10th constituency (second term, gave up the seat to stay in government)
Minister of National Education and Youth
Prime Minister (resignation accepted 16 July 2024, caretaker until 5 September 2024)
President of the Ensemble pour la République group, Assemblée nationale

delivery.what: Abaya and qamis ban in public schools (Education Minister, announced late August 2023, applied from the September 2023 school start)
delivery.assessment: The government presented it as a secularism (laïcité) measure. According to Wikipedia, 67 pupils were refused entry at the school start. Left-wing parties and Muslim organisations objected. It is often cited as a defining act of his time at Education. Only encyclopedic sources were checked, so this lacks a multi-outlet assessment from different leanings.

delivery.what: 'Choc des savoirs' education reform, announced December 2023 (including level-based groups in 6e and 5e) and a school-uniform experiment in about 10 schools, announced autumn 2023
delivery.assessment: Both were launched under his authority as Education Minister and then as PM. According to Wikipedia, the level-based groups were dropped about two years later as ineffective and the uniform experiment was abandoned in summer 2026. Later governments made both decisions. No primary or second source was found for the outcome, so the result is reported only, without a verdict.

delivery.what: Premiership (9 January - 16 July 2024, then caretaker until 5 September 2024)
delivery.assessment: He started with a 15-member government on 11 January 2024, which grew to 35 members on 8 February 2024. Several ministers had served under Nicolas Sarkozy or came from UMP/LR. English Wikipedia says many outlets called it the most right-leaning cabinet of Macron's tenure. Ensemble came third with 20.0% in the first round of the 30 June 2024 legislative elections. Attal later said eight months had been too little time to see his plans through.

delivery.what: Agricultural and environmental decisions as PM (early 2024)
delivery.assessment: According to English Wikipedia, his government suspended and then modified the Ecophyto pesticide-reduction plan after pressure from farmers, and cut environmental budget lines including the Green Fund. Environmental groups and the left criticised these moves. No statement of the government's rationale and no source from another leaning was retrieved, so this is one-sided.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not researched: no left-leaning outlet could be consulted. Wikipedia reports that the left criticised the abaya ban and the 2024 environmental rollbacks.
media_portrayal.right_media: Not researched: no right-leaning outlet could be consulted.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Not researched beyond encyclopedic summaries. English Wikipedia reports that early in his premiership he was described as one of France's most popular politicians.
